facebook.long_form:
The AUSL All-Star Cup Series 3 draft is happening TOMORROW — and the strategic chess match is already underway.

Captains Ricketts, Coffey, and Netz each face a different kind of pressure when they step to the board at Parkway Bank Sports Complex in Rosemont on Thursday.

Here's the thing about the AUSL format that makes the draft so compelling: every pick has two layers. You're building a team you need to WIN with — but you're also managing individual point implications. Do you draft your biggest rival in the individual standings to control them? Or do you ignore them and focus purely on building a winning lineup?

Kowalik sits at No. 1 in the individual standings heading into Series 3. Romero surged +42 points in Series 2. Lemley climbed +26. The individual title is still very much alive, and it all comes down to Series 3 and Series 4 before the championship is awarded Aug 30.

Series 3 tips off Sunday, Aug 24. The draft is tomorrow. If you're a fan of the athletes and the format, this is the moment to pay attention.

Who do you think wins the individual title? 🥎

stories.title: September 1 Countdown — 12 Days, Final Prep Phase
stories.angle: With 12 days remaining, Class of 2028 recruits are in the final preparation window. Yesterday's angle covered the pre-Sept 1 checklist. Today: the mental and strategic preparation for when the phones start ringing — how to handle multiple simultaneous offers, how to evaluate a school's pitch, and why the first 48 hours will likely decide more than the next 3 months.

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text: 12 days to September 1. Class of 2028: rank your schools NOW. The phones ring fast once the window opens — sometimes within 48 hours. Recruits who know their answer before Sept 1 handle the pressure. Those who don't often rush into decisions they regret. 🥎

facebook.long_form:
12 days until September 1 — and for the Class of 2028, the hardest part isn't the recruiting process. It's knowing what to do when the phones start ringing all at once.

Here's what experienced recruiting families will tell you: the first 48 hours after Sept 1 are unlike anything you've prepared for. Coaches are calling the same recruits. Multiple schools may be offering at the same time. Commitment decisions that felt distant suddenly feel urgent.

The recruits who handle this well are the ones who made their decisions BEFORE the window opened — not during.

That means: rank your schools now. Know which campus felt right. Know what you value most: coaching philosophy, program culture, academics, location. Talk to your family. Have a framework.

You don't have to commit the first week. But the recruits who rush in without a plan often make decisions they later question. The ones who prepared are calm when the phones ring.

12 days. The window is coming. Are you ready? 🥎

article.headline: 12 Days to September 1: The Quiet Before the Storm for Class of 2028 Softball Recruits

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: 23 days until USA Softball opens WBSC World Cup group play in OKC. Group C: Netherlands (No. 6), Mexico (No. 7), China (No. 8). Top 2 teams advance to Brisbane — the LA28 Olympic qualifier. Devon Park, Sept 12-16. 🇺🇸 #USASoftball

facebook.long_form:
23 days until Team USA opens WBSC World Cup group play in Oklahoma City — and Group C is loaded.

The official 16-player roster is locked. Four Oklahoma Sooners (Alyssa Brito, Jayda Coleman, Tiare Jennings, Kelly Maxwell) lead the way. Veterans Rachel Garcia and Dejah Mulipola bring 2020 Olympic experience. Seven players from the 2025 World Games gold medal team round out a deep squad.

Group C opponents:
• Netherlands — No. 6 in the world
• Mexico — No. 7
• China — No. 8

Top two teams advance to the Brisbane Finals (April 5–11, 2027) — the direct path to LA28 Olympic qualification.

USA is No. 1. This should be their tournament to advance — but the group isn't a layup. Netherlands and China are both capable of pulling off an upset.

Games begin Sept 12 at Devon Park in Oklahoma City. If you're in the area — this is a must-see. 🇺🇸

article.headline: USA Softball Faces Netherlands, Mexico, and China in Oklahoma City — 23 Days Out

stories.title: Oklahoma Softball — Portal Rebuild Continues, 11 Days to Deadline
stories.angle: The August 31 transfer portal deadline is 11 days away. OU has already added Macie Harter and secured its 4th 2027 verbal commitment with Ori Mailo (No. 4 overall) on campus, Payton Westra (No. 2 overall recruit) committed. Key departures: Kasidi Pickering (→ Texas Tech), Tia Milloy. The story is how Gasso is aggressively rebuilding after their first WCWS miss since 2015.

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: Transfer portal closes in 11 days (Aug 31). Oklahoma has added Macie Harter, secured Payton Westra (No. 2 overall) and Ori Mailo (No. 4 overall) in its 2027 class. Patty Gasso is rebuilding after OU's first WCWS miss since 2015. #OUSoftball

facebook.long_form:
The transfer portal closes in 11 days — and Oklahoma softball is making the most of every hour.

Patty Gasso is rebuilding after the Sooners' first WCWS miss since 2015, and the moves she's made this summer paint a picture of a program determined to bounce back fast.

Additions: Macie Harter joins via the transfer portal. The 2027 recruiting class is taking serious shape — Payton Westra (No. 2 overall) and Ori Mailo (No. 4 overall, who was already on campus this past season) headline a class that also includes pitchers, infielders, and outfielders across multiple signing periods.

Losses: Kasidi Pickering departed for Texas Tech. Tia Milloy transferred out. Those are significant names to lose in one cycle.

But Gasso has rebuilt before. The Sooners won three straight WCWS titles (2021–23) before falling short in 2025 and 2026.

Aug 31 is the deadline. Watch for any last-minute additions as programs finalize their rosters for the fall semester.

article.headline: Oklahoma's Roster Revolution: Portal Deadline Looms as Gasso Builds for 2027

stories.title: Texas Softball — Fall Camp, Three-Peat Roster Takes Shape
stories.angle: With fall camp underway and 11 new additions in a 24-player roster — including a former OU pitcher via transfer — Texas's path to a third straight WCWS title is coming into focus. Teagan Kavan (2x WCWS MOP, first in history) returns as the anchor. Only UCLA (1988–90) and OU (2021–23) have won three straight WCWS. Texas finished 49-12 in 2026.

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: Texas softball fall camp is underway. 24 players, 11 new additions, Teagan Kavan back as 2x WCWS MOP. Only UCLA (1988-90) and Oklahoma (2021-23) have won 3 straight WCWS. The Longhorns are trying to join that list. #HookEm #TexasSoftball

facebook.long_form:
Texas softball's fall camp is underway — and the roster they're putting on the field in 2027 is starting to take shape.

24 players. 11 new additions. A former Oklahoma pitcher added through the transfer portal. And Teagan Kavan back as the unquestioned anchor of the staff — the first player ever to win WCWS Most Outstanding Player twice.

The question everyone in the sport is asking: can the Longhorns become only the third program in history to win three straight Women's College World Series titles?

The answer won't come until Oklahoma City in June 2027. But the roster they're assembling suggests Texas isn't treating this like a team just trying to maintain. They're trying to be the best team in the country again — for the third time in a row.

For context: only UCLA (1988–90) and Oklahoma (2021–23) have ever done it. Texas would join that list as just the third program ever.

Fall camp. New roster. Same standard. 🤘

article.headline: Texas Softball's Three-Peat Roster Is Coming Into Focus at Fall Camp
